old: This state is named for what it removes, not what it adds — a total blank where perception used to be.
Its Greek root literally means 'without sensation,' built from a prefix for 'not' and a word for 'sensation.'
It shares that sensation-root with words describing the ability to perceive or feel — just with the negative stuck on front.
clues: This state of the body once meant any general lack of feeling, and for more than a century and a half in English it had nothing to do with doctors.
Doctors bring it on deliberately with drugs or gases so a patient feels no pain during surgery, a controlled loss of sensation rather than mere numbness or ordinary sleep.
Before an operation you may be offered it in general or local form; its ancient Greek source meant simply 'without sensation.'
